title: Frenzy for Solar Eclipse Glasses Takes Over London
partialText: Ahead of Wednesday’s rare cosmic event, thousands of people in London are searching for protective eyewear, as prices surge and stocks sell out.

title: G.M.’s ‘Car Guy’ Talks Electrics, China and Nepotism
partialText: Mark Reuss became the automaker’s president seven years ago, ascending to a role his father was fired from decades before. We got the chance to speak with him.

title: Robots That Walk and Talk Are Coming to Car Factories
partialText: But experts warn they may not deliver the gains in efficiency that proponents claim.

title: Ari Emanuel’s Company to Acquire 7 Broadway Theaters and 10 in the West End
partialText: The purchase of ATG Entertainment, which operates dozens of venues worldwide, will require regulatory approval.

title: The Perils of Wall St.’s Race to Pour Billions More Into A.I.
partialText: Investors including BlackRock have committed an eye-popping amount to lend to the artificial intelligence industry. That enthusiasm isn’t shared by everyone.

title: Oil Prices Touch $90 a Barrel Over U.S.-Iran Stalemate
partialText: The stalemate over the Iran war hardened and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continued to dwindle.

title: Heat, Fire, Smoke and Storms Are Wreaking Havoc on the Economy
partialText: Repeated heat waves, wildfires, droughts and storms are solidifying the understanding that new investments are unavoidable.

title: How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco
partialText: A wave of disinformation online contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta who were trying to reach Europe, resulting in about 90 deaths.

title: Should You Be Dating While Unemployed?
partialText: If you’re single and unemployed, it may make sense to prioritize job hunting. But that doesn’t have to mean putting your life on pause.

title: As Credit Card Debt Mounts, Home Becomes a Piggy Bank
partialText: A rise in home equity to record levels has led many Americans to refinance their mortgages to pay their bills.

title: Wall St. Wants Another Half-Trillion Dollars for the A.I. Boom
partialText: Six giant investment firms announced a $500 billion effort to raise money for customers of Nvidia to pay for computing power.

title: Traffic to Trump’s Truth Social Falls Sharply This Summer
partialText: President Trump’s social media platform has had double-digit declines in visitors in June and July, according to estimates from a widely cited online tracking firm.

title: Trump Shrugs Off A.I. and Data Center Concerns as Voters Grow Anxious
partialText: The president and his top aides have been especially bullish about data centers, despite national blowback against the facilities.

title: How Small, Independent Newspapers Are Still Finding Readers
partialText: In a world of failing newspapers, free weeklies like The Chronicle of Glens Falls, N.Y., are still finding readers. All it takes is owners who do absolutely everything.

title: Waymo Is Growing Faster Than Ever. So Are Its ‘Edge Cases.’
partialText: As Waymo deploys more driverless cars to 15 U.S. cities and counting, its vehicles keep encountering new and unexpected situations that they have no script to handle.

title: Why Meta Is Betting Big on Open A.I.
partialText: The technology giant is embracing open models, closer ties to Washington and more as it seeks to catch up in the artificial intelligence race.

title: Boeing to Sell 3 Autonomous Flight Subsidiaries
partialText: In exchange for the sale to Archer Aviation, which is developing a piloted electric aircraft, Boeing will receive a 16.5 percent stake in Archer.

title: Private Equity Is Stuck With 33,575 Unsold Businesses
partialText: Even amid a booming deal-making environment, private equity firms are unable to exit a growing number of investments at values their investors require.

title: Can A.I. Get You Where You Want to Go for Less?
partialText: A wave of new services uses A.I. to monitor flights and hotel reservations to help you find lower prices. We look at how these tools work.

title: Flock Cameras Are Dividing U.S. Cities. Here’s What to Know About Them.
partialText: Flock Safety’s automated license plate-reading cameras, used by thousands of law enforcement agencies in the U.S., have drawn intense criticism from civil liberties groups.

title: Taylor Farms Voluntarily Recalls Fresh Jalapeños Over Salmonella Concerns
partialText: The company said it was unaware of any reported illnesses linked to its products containing jalapeños, which were distributed to major retailers across 26 states.

title: Oil Prices Climb on Stalemate in Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Hopes were dashed over the weekend for a breakthrough on shipping traffic through the critical waterway in the Persian Gulf.

title: Flight Is Canceled After a Child Refuses to Be Seated
partialText: Passengers aboard a Porter Airlines plane headed to Toronto had to wait for a flight the next day after a child remained standing in a seat and would not get buckled in, the company said.

title: Kalshi’s Tarek Mansour Isn’t Interested in Management Advice
partialText: Tarek Mansour co-founded the fast-growing prediction market company shortly after graduating from M.I.T., aiming to provide a “mathematical, objective” view of the world.

title: A Maine Town, Once Dependent on a Paper Mill, Tries to Move On
partialText: For over a century, Madison Paper Industries was a small Maine town’s economic engine. A new owner moved in, but uncertainty persists.

title: MacKenzie Scott Steps Back Into Spotlight With New Book
partialText: She posted four pages of a manuscript on a newly started Substack newsletter on Saturday and said that the novel would be released serially throughout August.

title: Think It’s Cool to Wear Fancy Sneakers to Work? You Might Be Old.
partialText: After years of office casual, young people are embracing loafers, derbies and oxfords.

title: Medicare Advantage’s Perks Are Getting Scrutiny
partialText: Officials said no to health plans that wanted to expand extra benefits to cover medical marijuana, streaming services and shopping clubs. More changes are coming in 2027.

title: How an N.F.L.-Backed Plan to Revitalize Canton, Ohio, Faltered
partialText: The “Hall of Fame Village” was pitched in 2014 as a boon to the city. But hundreds of millions were spent, the N.F.L. backed out, and the project is unfinished.

title: Can Netflix Save a Summer Slump With a Stunt on Sunset Boulevard?
partialText: The streaming giant, still looking for this year’s blockbuster, paid an actor to spend three days inside a billboard in Los Angeles to promote an upcoming film.

title: Canada Offers U.S. Concessions in Trade Talks but Demands a Comprehensive Deal
partialText: Prime Minister Mark Carney is attempting to prevent 50 percent tariffs against many Canadian goods scheduled for this month.

title: Trump Restarts Battle to Fire Sitting Fed Governor Lisa Cook
partialText: The Trump administration, rebuffed by the Supreme Court in its first attempt to fire Lisa D. Cook, sent the Federal Reserve governor a letter saying it was “considering” removing her from the job.

title: Weak Jobs Report Does Not Eliminate Prospects of Interest Rate Rise
partialText: Officials at the Federal Reserve are chiefly focused on the trajectory of inflation after five years of overshooting the central bank’s 2 percent target.

title: If You’re Struggling to Pay Day-to-Day Bills, There’s Help
partialText: Nonprofit financial counselors say there has been a significant increase this year in the number of borrowers seeking their advice.

title: The Bond Market Is Signaling Rising Risks. Investors Should Listen.
partialText: While the Fed didn’t raise rates, the bond market did. That means hardship for home buyers and higher hurdles for A.I. data centers and the stock market. But it’s also a boon for retirees.

title: Jobs Report Poses New Test for Warsh and the Fed
partialText: Friday’s jobs report comes as investors increasingly expect the Federal Reserve to begin raising interest rates as soon as next month.

title: Labor Market Shifts Into Reverse as Employers Balk at Hiring
partialText: A spring surge rapidly faded as the summer brought higher prices and more uncertainty for businesses, even as they avoided layoffs.

title: Pope Leo XIV Was Elected. The Chicago White Sox Were Resurrected.
partialText: The elevation of Pope Leo XIV, a Chicago native and lifelong supporter of the Sox, was a godsend for a team failing on the field and with fans.

title: How to Plan an African Safari
partialText: From budgeting to timing your trip, here’s what to consider before you go.

title: China’s Export Boom Rolls On Despite Trade Backlash
partialText: China’s factories are finding eager buyers abroad even as weak consumer spending and a prolonged property slump weigh on growth at home.

title: FIFA Executives Were Given Ultimatum to Approve World Cup Privatization Plan
partialText: The day before the World Cup final, key FIFA figures faced a stunning demand to sign off on a multibillion-dollar privatization project.

title: Amid Cyclospora Outbreak, Demand for Locally Grown Lettuce Surges
partialText: Small produce stands and farmers’ markets are seeing a surge in demand for leafy greens as sales of lettuce and salad kits from grocery chains and big retailers drop.

title: Drought Threatens a Vital Economic Artery in the Heart of Europe
partialText: The Rhine conveys vessels and cargo that power European industry. Record low water levels are disrupting supply chains, adding costs and presenting fresh risks to growth.

title: A Promising Heart Drug Fails, Challenging a Long-Held Theory of Disease
partialText: The drug targeted inflammation, and its shocking failure has experts questioning whether inflammation really does cause heart disease.

title: China’s Unitree Prices IPO in Bet Investors Are Ready for Humanoid Robots
partialText: Unitree Robotics wants to raise about $900 million in an I.P.O. that tests market interest in humanoid robots, a technology that wows but has yet to prove its viability.

title: The ‘Heated Rivalry’ Star Hudson Williams Uplifts a Canadian Tire Bag
partialText: After the actor Hudson Williams was photographed carrying a plaid reusable shopping bag, priced under $2, the tote has become a viral fashion accessory.

title: What’s Behind the A.I. Shake-Up at Google
partialText: A new role for Demis Hassabis, the head of Google’s artificial intelligence unit, reflects reality at the tech giant. Investors remain worried.

title: Follow the Markets and Track Stocks With These Free Apps
partialText: Google Finance and Apple’s Stocks app have added new features over the years to make them more useful for tracking the markets and your investments.

title: Why So Many C.E.O.s Are Getting a Chief of Staff
partialText: The position as a trusted sounding board is in high demand as business gets more complex — and everyone wants to get in on the latest bureaucratic fad.

title: F.D.A. Approves Moderna’s mRNA Flu Vaccine
partialText: The agency had initially refused to even review the application but reversed course after a public outcry.
